A 1-trillion-parameter model that only runs a fraction of itself per token. Here's how Mistral Large 4 is built. 🧵

Most launch posts focus on benchmarks. I went through the architecture of Mistral's new open-weight model instead, and several design choices are worth a look.

**🧠 Two kinds of sparsity working together**
• **Experts:** 71 of the 72 decoder layers are MoE. A softmax router picks 4 of 128 experts per token, plus 1 shared expert that always runs. The first layer stays dense.
• **Attention:** Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) keeps a compressed KV cache, and a DeepSeek Sparse Attention indexer selects up to 2,048 earlier positions for each query.

In short, one mechanism decides *which weights* run and the other decides *which context* matters. That combination is how it reaches a 1M-token context window without the compute cost exploding.

**📐 Positional encoding choices**
• A 3:1 RoPE-to-NoPE pattern: every fourth layer has no positional encoding at all
• "LeRope": YaRN-scaled RoPE with one *learned* multiplier per frequency
• KV state shared across layers

**👁️ Vision**
A 1.6B Pixtral encoder (30 layers, 14×14 patches, spatial merge of 2) feeds images into the language model.

**⚡ How it performs in practice**
On 8× H200 via Hugging Face Inference Endpoints:
• ~0.6s time to first token on a 1K-token prompt
• ~65 tok/s generation, rising to 120–138 tok/s when the built-in DSpark draft head's speculative tokens are accepted
• ~480 tok/s aggregate across 1,000 concurrent ShareGPT conversations

One quirk to note: reasoning can't be turned off. You choose low, medium, or high effort, and high is the default.

The results back up the design. It's the #5 open-weights model on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and scored a record 82% on reproduce-and-patch vulnerability tasks.

MoE plus sparse attention plus MLA is looking like the standard recipe for frontier open models. Which part of this design do you think matters most? 👇
